report.name: Database Health Check
report.description: Complete Oracle database health check: identification, patches, parameters, memory, performance, SQL, schema objects, storage, backup/Data Guard, security and alert log — in customer-deliverable report format.
report.analysis_instructions:
IDIOMA: escreva TODO o relatório em português (pt-BR). Não traduza jargão técnico consagrado (tablespace, redo log, standby, grant, bind variable, health check etc.).

The line above defines the report's OUTPUT LANGUAGE. EVERYTHING in the report is written in that language: prose, table headers, the fixed labels ("Recommendation:", "Verified with no findings:") and EVERY section title. The English titles and labels in this specification are meant to be TRANSLATED into the output language, never copied verbatim — e.g. with Portuguese output, "## 1. Database Analysis" is rendered "## 1. Análise do Banco de Dados". Only untranslatable technical jargon stays in English. Numbering, order and meaning never change.

This is a formal HEALTH CHECK for customer delivery. Every execution must produce the SAME structure, in this exact order, with these numbered titles. Each query's description starts with a tag [4] or [5.x] naming the section where it must be handled — respect that mapping.

FORMAT (Markdown): each section 1-6 title as a level-2 heading ("## 1. …"); subsections 4.x and 5.x as level-3 headings ("### 5.1 …"), title text always in the output language. Blank line between titles, paragraphs, lists and tables. Tables ALWAYS as complete Markdown — header row, |---|---| separator line and one line per record; never loose '|' cells in running text. The identification in section 4.1 must be a table in this format.

1. Database Analysis (Portuguese title: Análise do Banco de Dados) — opening that identifies the database (name, version, platform, CPUs, memory, size — from the "System Under Observation - Database" query) and the goal: report opportunities to improve configuration and performance and reduce the risk of downtime.

2. Executive Summary (Portuguese title: Sumário Executivo) — overview of the database's state, then the benefits list: an intro line saying that applying this report's recommendations can lead to the items that follow (English output: "If applied, the recommendations in this report can lead to:" · Portuguese output: "Se aplicadas, as recomendações deste relatório podem levar a:" · other languages: translate it), followed by benefits derived from THIS run's findings.

3. Action Items Summary (Portuguese title: Resumo de Itens de Ação) — short bullets with ALL actions recommended in section 5, in the same order they appear there. No item may exist here without existing in section 5, and vice versa.

4. System Under Observation (Portuguese title: Sistema Sob Observação) — 4.1 Database (Portuguese title: Banco de dados): the identification table; 4.2 Options enabled/disabled and Features used (Portuguese title: Options habilitadas/desabilitadas e Features usadas): summarize, and include a note in the output language saying this is not a licensing report, only the current state; 4.3 Observation window (Portuguese title: Janela de observação): what the data covers — current state, caches and history available at collection time.

5. Findings and Recommendations (Portuguese title: Achados e Recomendações) — subsections ALWAYS in this order, ALL present even without findings:
5.1 Patches and version · 5.2 Database parameters · 5.3 Memory (SGA/PGA and advisors) · 5.4 Performance and statistics · 5.5 SQL efficiency (literals, cursors, parse) · 5.6 Schema objects and indexes · 5.7 Storage · 5.8 Backup, recovery and Data Guard · 5.9 Security and auditing · 5.10 Alert Log
(Portuguese output renders these subsection titles as: 5.1 Patches e versão · 5.2 Parâmetros de banco · 5.3 Memória (SGA/PGA e advisors) · 5.4 Performance e estatísticas · 5.5 Eficiência de SQL (literals, cursors, parse) · 5.6 Objetos de schema e índices · 5.7 Storage · 5.8 Backup, recovery e Data Guard · 5.9 Segurança e auditoria · 5.10 Alert Log. Other languages: translate the English titles the same way.)

Within each subsection:
- For each real problem: (a) what was observed, citing real numbers and objects from the results; (b) why it is a problem and what it can cause — educate the reader, like a senior consultant; (c) a closing recommendation line with the concrete action, labeled in the output language (English: "Recommendation:" · Portuguese: "Recomendação:"). Order by severity: downtime/data-loss risk > performance > housekeeping.
- After the findings, close with one line listing that subsection's checks that came back clean, labeled in the output language (English: "Verified with no findings:" · Portuguese: "Verificado sem apontamentos:"). A fully clean subsection = only that line.
- A clean check never gets the (a)(b)(c) format: only that closing clean-checks line.
- An empty result means "no problem" only when the query's description says so; for inventories (RMAN backups, redo, archive destinations) empty is a FINDING.
- A query marked "NOT COLLECTED" never counts as verified: handle it in section 6.
- Memory recommendations only from the advisors (estimated factors); if the curve shows irrelevant gain, state that the current size is adequate.
- Recommend nothing without evidence in the results. Never invent values.

6. Queries not collected (Portuguese title: Consultas não coletadas) — list each "NOT COLLECTED" query with its ORA error and the likely cause (missing grant/feature). If there are none, say in one line, in the output language, that all queries were collected successfully.

Final rules: use exclusively this run's results; operating-system items (kernel, OS limits) are not collected — do not invent them; never mention other customers, databases or previous runs; professional, direct, didactic tone.

sqls.name: System Under Observation - Database
sqls.description: [4] Database identification: name, version, host, size, memory, CPUs, OS. Feeds the opening (section 1) and section 4.1.
sqls.sql:
WITH /* 1a.1 */
rac AS (
    SELECT /*+ MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE */
           COUNT(*) instances,
           CASE COUNT(*) WHEN 1 THEN 'Single-instance'
                ELSE COUNT(*) || '-node RAC cluster' END db_type
    FROM gv$instance
),
mem AS (SELECT /*+ MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE */ SUM(value) target
          FROM gv$system_parameter2 WHERE name = 'memory_target'),
sga AS (SELECT /*+ MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE */ SUM(value) target
          FROM gv$system_parameter2 WHERE name = 'sga_target'),
pga AS (SELECT /*+ MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE */ SUM(value) target
          FROM gv$system_parameter2 WHERE name = 'pga_aggregate_target'),
db_block AS (SELECT /*+ MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE */ value bytes
               FROM gv$system_parameter2 WHERE name = 'db_block_size'),
db AS (SELECT /*+ MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE */ name, platform_name FROM v$database),
pdbs AS (SELECT /*+ MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE */ name, open_mode FROM v$pdbs),
inst AS (SELECT /*+ MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE */ host_name, version db_version FROM v$instance),
data AS (SELECT /*+ MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE */ SUM(bytes) bytes, COUNT(*) files,
                COUNT(DISTINCT ts#) tablespaces FROM v$datafile),
temp AS (SELECT /*+ MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE */ SUM(bytes) bytes FROM v$tempfile),
log AS (SELECT /*+ MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE */ SUM(bytes) * MAX(members) bytes FROM v$log),
control AS (SELECT /*+ MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE */ SUM(block_size * file_size_blks) bytes
              FROM v$controlfile),
core AS (SELECT /*+ MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE */ SUM(value) cnt
           FROM gv$osstat WHERE stat_name = 'NUM_CPU_CORES'),
cpu AS (SELECT /*+ MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE */ SUM(value) cnt
          FROM gv$osstat WHERE stat_name = 'NUM_CPUS'),
pmem AS (SELECT /*+ MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE */ SUM(value) bytes
           FROM gv$osstat WHERE stat_name = 'PHYSICAL_MEMORY_BYTES')
SELECT 'Database name:' system_item, db.name system_value FROM db
UNION ALL
SELECT 'PDB: ' || name, 'Open mode: ' || open_mode FROM pdbs
UNION ALL
SELECT 'Oracle Database version:', inst.db_version FROM inst
UNION ALL
SELECT 'Host name:', inst.host_name FROM inst
UNION ALL
SELECT 'Database block size:',
       TRIM(TO_CHAR(db_block.bytes / POWER(2,10), '90')) || ' KB' FROM db_block
UNION ALL
SELECT 'Database size:',
       TRIM(TO_CHAR(ROUND((data.bytes + temp.bytes + log.bytes + control.bytes)
            / POWER(10,12), 3), '999,999,990.000')) || ' TB'
  FROM data, temp, log, control
UNION ALL
SELECT 'Datafiles:', data.files || ' (on ' || data.tablespaces || ' tablespaces)' FROM data
UNION ALL
SELECT 'Instance configuration:', rac.db_type FROM rac
UNION ALL
SELECT 'Database memory:',
       CASE WHEN mem.target > 0 THEN 'MEMORY ' ||
            TRIM(TO_CHAR(ROUND(mem.target / POWER(2,30), 1), '999,990.0')) || ' GB, ' END ||
       CASE WHEN sga.target > 0 THEN 'SGA ' ||
            TRIM(TO_CHAR(ROUND(sga.target / POWER(2,30), 1), '999,990.0')) || ' GB, ' END ||
       CASE WHEN pga.target > 0 THEN 'PGA ' ||
            TRIM(TO_CHAR(ROUND(pga.target / POWER(2,30), 1), '999,990.0')) || ' GB, ' END ||
       CASE WHEN mem.target > 0 THEN 'AMM'
            ELSE CASE WHEN sga.target > 0 THEN 'ASMM' ELSE 'MANUAL' END END
  FROM mem, sga, pga
UNION ALL
SELECT 'Physical CPUs:', core.cnt || ' cores, on ' || rac.db_type FROM rac, core
UNION ALL
SELECT 'Oracle CPUs:', cpu.cnt || ' CPUs (threads), on ' || rac.db_type FROM rac, cpu
UNION ALL
SELECT 'Physical RAM:',
       TRIM(TO_CHAR(ROUND(pmem.bytes / POWER(2,30), 1), '999,990.0')) || ' GB, on ' || rac.db_type
  FROM rac, pmem
UNION ALL
SELECT 'Operating system:', db.platform_name FROM db;

sqls.name: Database Features Used
sqls.description: [4] Features already used (dba_feature_usage_statistics, summary with dates). In 5.9, flag pack features (AWR, Tuning Advisor) used if the edition/parameters suggest a missing license.
sqls.sql:
SELECT
    d.name,
    x.name,
    x.detected_usages,
    x.currently_used,
    x.first_usage_date,
    x.last_usage_date,
    x.description
FROM
    dba_feature_usage_statistics x
    left join v$database d on d.dbid = x.dbid
WHERE
    d.name is not null
ORDER BY
    x.name,
    x.version;

	   --,c.name con_name

sqls.name: Non-default Init Parameters
sqls.description: [5.2] Non-default parameters (per thread) — the main input for the parameter analysis. Judge values against best practices for the version/edition (e.g. recyclebin OFF, fast_start_mttr_target, filesystemio_options, cursor_sharing, processes vs sessions).
sqls.sql:
SELECT num, '*' "THREAD#", name, value /* 2e.222 */
  FROM v$PARAMETER WHERE NUM IN (
SELECT num
  FROM v$parameter
 WHERE (isdefault = 'FALSE' OR ismodified <> 'FALSE')
   AND name NOT LIKE 'nls%'
 MINUS
SELECT num
  FROM gv$parameter gvp, gv$instance gvi
 WHERE num IN (
SELECT DISTINCT gvpa.num
  FROM gv$parameter gvpa, gv$parameter gvpb
 WHERE gvpa.num = gvpb.num
   AND  gvpa.value <> gvpb.value
   AND (gvpa.isdefault = 'FALSE' OR gvpa.ismodified <> 'FALSE')
   AND gvpa.name NOT LIKE 'nls%')
   AND gvi.inst_id = gvp.inst_id
   AND (gvp.isdefault = 'FALSE' OR gvp.ismodified <> 'FALSE')
   AND gvp.name NOT LIKE 'nls%')
 UNION
SELECT num, TO_CHAR(thread#) "THREAD#", name, value
  FROM gv$parameter gvp, gv$instance gvi
 WHERE num IN (
SELECT DISTINCT gvpa.num
  FROM gv$parameter gvpa, gv$parameter gvpb
 WHERE gvpa.num = gvpb.num
   AND gvpa.value <> gvpb.value
   AND (gvpa.isdefault = 'FALSE' OR gvpa.ismodified <> 'FALSE')
   AND gvp.name NOT LIKE 'nls%')
   AND gvi.inst_id = gvp.inst_id
   AND (gvp.isdefault = 'FALSE' OR gvp.ismodified <> 'FALSE')
   AND gvp.name NOT LIKE 'nls%'
 ORDER BY 1, 2;

sqls.name: Modified parameters
sqls.description: [5.2] Parameters changed at runtime (ISMODIFIED). Memory vs spfile divergence deserves a note.
sqls.sql:
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 1a.21 */
       x.*
	   --,c.name con_name
  FROM gv$system_parameter2 x
       --LEFT OUTER JOIN v$containers c ON c.con_id = x.con_id
 WHERE x.ismodified = 'MODIFIED'
 ORDER BY
       --x.con_id,
       x.name,
       x.inst_id,
       x.ordinal;

sqls.name: All parameters (raw)
sqls.description: [5.2] Full gv$system_parameter2 dump for human reference; base the parameter analysis on the non-default/modified queries, not on this sample.
sqls.sql:
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 1a.22 */
       x.*
	   --,c.name con_name
  FROM gv$system_parameter2 x
       --LEFT OUTER JOIN v$containers c ON c.con_id = x.con_id
 ORDER BY
       --x.con_id,
       x.name,
       x.inst_id,
       x.ordinal;

sqls.name: Parallel Parameters
sqls.description: [5.2] parallel% parameters including hidden ones (requires an X$ grant; may fail). Check parallel_max_servers/threshold coherence against the CPUs in section 4.
sqls.sql:
select name, description, value, isdefault, ismodified, isset
from
(
select flag,name,value,isdefault,ismodified,
case when isdefault||ismodified = 'TRUEFALSE' then 'FALSE' else 'TRUE' end isset ,
description
from
   (
       select
            decode(substr(i.ksppinm,1,1),'_',2,1) flag
            , i.ksppinm name
            , sv.ksppstvl value
            , sv.ksppstdf  isdefault
--            , decode(bitand(sv.ksppstvf,7),1,'MODIFIED',4,'SYSTEM_MOD','FALSE') ismodified
            , decode(bitand(sv.ksppstvf,7),1,'TRUE',4,'TRUE','FALSE') ismodified
, i.KSPPDESC description
         from sys.x$ksppi  i
            , sys.x$ksppsv sv
        where i.indx = sv.indx
   )
)
where name like nvl('%parallel%',name)
and flag != 3
order by flag,replace(name,'_','');

sqls.name: Result Cache parameters
sqls.description: [5.2] Result cache parameters.
sqls.sql:
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 3d.272 */
       inst_id, name "PARAMETER", value, isdefault, ismodified
  FROM gv$system_parameter2
 WHERE name IN ('result_cache_mode','result_cache_max_size','result_cache_max_result')
 ORDER BY 2,1,3;

sqls.name: Result Cache status
sqls.description: [5.2] Result cache status (may fail without EXECUTE on DBMS_RESULT_CACHE).
sqls.sql: SELECT dbms_result_cache.status FROM dual;

sqls.name: Memory Dynamic Components
sqls.description: [5.3] Current memory component sizes (gv$memory_dynamic_components).

sqls.name: Memory Resize Operations
sqls.description: [5.3] Recent resize operations; frequent resizes between buffer cache and shared pool = memory pressure (a finding).
sqls.sql:
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 1d.55 */
       *
  FROM gv$memory_resize_ops
 ORDER BY
       inst_id,
       start_time DESC,
       component;

sqls.name: Memory Target Advice
sqls.description: [5.3] memory_target advisor (empty when AMM is off). A lower ESTD_DB_TIME_FACTOR at a larger size = real gain.

sqls.name: SGA Target Advice
sqls.description: [5.3] SGA advisor: find where ESTD_PHYSICAL_READS stops dropping. Recommend an increase only with a clear gain AND physical RAM available (section 4).

sqls.name: PGA Target Advice
sqls.description: [5.3] PGA advisor: ESTD_OVERALLOC_COUNT > 0 = undersized PGA (a finding); recommend the size where overallocation reaches zero and the cache hit stabilizes.

sqls.name: System Wait Class
sqls.description: [5.4] Cumulative time per wait class SINCE STARTUP (not a window). Describe the profile (CPU vs User I/O vs Commit...) with that caveat stated. Ignore the Idle class (not real waiting).
sqls.sql:
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 3d.271 */
       x.*
  FROM gv$system_wait_class x
 ORDER BY
       --x.con_id,
	   x.inst_id,
       x.time_waited DESC;

sqls.name: Tables with Outdated Stats
sqls.description: [5.4] Application tables with statistics older than 31 days. A large volume = deficient gathering, bad-plan risk; recommend reviewing the window/auto task.
sqls.sql:
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 3c.260 */
       --s.con_id,
	   s.owner, s.table_name, s.num_rows, s.last_analyzed, s.stale_stats, s.stattype_locked
	   --,c.name con_name
  FROM dba_tab_statistics s,
       dba_tables t
	   --LEFT OUTER JOIN v$containers c ON c.con_id = t.con_id
 WHERE s.object_type = 'TABLE'
   AND s.owner NOT IN ('ANONYMOUS','APEX_030200','APEX_040000','APEX_040200','APEX_180200','APEX_SSO','APPQOSSYS','CTXSYS','DBSNMP','DIP','EXFSYS','FLOWS_FILES','MDSYS','OLAPSYS','ORACLE_OCM','ORDDATA','ORDPLUGINS','ORDSYS','OUTLN','OWBSYS')
   AND s.owner NOT IN ('SI_INFORMTN_SCHEMA','SQLTXADMIN','SQLTXPLAIN','SYS','SYSMAN','SYSTEM','TRCANLZR','WMSYS','XDB','XS$NULL','PERFSTAT','STDBYPERF','MGDSYS','OJVMSYS','GSMADMIN_INTERNAL')
   AND s.last_analyzed < SYSDATE - 31
   AND s.table_name NOT LIKE 'BIN%'
   AND NOT (s.table_name LIKE '%TEMP' OR s.table_name LIKE '%\_TEMP\_%' ESCAPE '\')
   --AND t.con_id = s.con_id
   AND t.owner = s.owner
   AND t.table_name = s.table_name
   AND t.temporary = 'N'
   AND NOT EXISTS (
SELECT NULL
  FROM dba_external_tables e
 WHERE e.owner = s.owner
   --AND e.con_id = s.con_id
   AND e.table_name = s.table_name
)
 ORDER BY
       --s.con_id,
       s.owner, s.table_name;

sqls.name: Tables with Locked Stats
sqls.description: [5.4] Tables with locked statistics; confirm whether the lock is intentional (e.g. volatile tables) or leftover.
sqls.sql:
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 3c.261 */
       --s.con_id,
	   s.owner, s.table_name, t.temporary, s.num_rows, s.last_analyzed, s.stale_stats, s.stattype_locked, e.type_name external_table_type
	   --,c.name con_name
  FROM dba_tab_statistics s
       LEFT OUTER JOIN dba_external_tables e ON e.owner = s.owner AND e.table_name = s.table_name --AND e.con_id = s.con_id
	   --LEFT OUTER JOIN v$containers c ON c.con_id = s.con_id
      ,dba_tables t
 WHERE s.object_type = 'TABLE'
   AND s.owner NOT IN ('ANONYMOUS','APEX_030200','APEX_040000','APEX_040200','APEX_180200','APEX_SSO','APPQOSSYS','CTXSYS','DBSNMP','DIP','EXFSYS','FLOWS_FILES','MDSYS','OLAPSYS','ORACLE_OCM','ORDDATA','ORDPLUGINS','ORDSYS','OUTLN','OWBSYS')
   AND s.owner NOT IN ('SI_INFORMTN_SCHEMA','SQLTXADMIN','SQLTXPLAIN','SYS','SYSMAN','SYSTEM','TRCANLZR','WMSYS','XDB','XS$NULL','PERFSTAT','STDBYPERF','MGDSYS','OJVMSYS','GSMADMIN_INTERNAL')
   AND s.stattype_locked IS NOT NULL
   AND s.table_name NOT LIKE 'BIN%'
   --AND t.con_id = s.con_id
   AND t.owner = s.owner
   AND t.table_name = s.table_name
 ORDER BY
       --s.con_id,
       s.owner, s.table_name;

sqls.name: Stats History Availability
sqls.description: [5.4] Statistics history availability/retention (stats restore).

sqls.name: DOP on tables
sqls.description: [5.4] Count of tables with fixed DOP > 1 or DEFAULT per owner. A fixed table DOP triggers unintended parallelism on any query; recommend review.
sqls.sql:
WITH x AS (
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 2a.90 */
       --con_id,
       owner,
       SUM(CASE WHEN TRIM(degree) = 'DEFAULT' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) "DEFAULT",
       SUM(CASE WHEN TRIM(degree) = '0' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) "0",
       SUM(CASE WHEN TRIM(degree) = '1' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) "1",
       SUM(CASE WHEN TRIM(degree) = '2' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) "2",
       SUM(CASE WHEN TRIM(degree) IN ('3', '4') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) "3-4",
       SUM(CASE WHEN TRIM(degree) IN ('5', '6', '7', '8') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) "5-8",
       SUM(CASE WHEN TRIM(degree) IN ('9', '10', '11', '12', '13', '14', '15', '16') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) "9-16",
       SUM(CASE WHEN LENGTH(TRIM(degree)) = 2 AND TRIM(degree) BETWEEN '17' AND '32' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) "17-32",
       SUM(CASE WHEN LENGTH(TRIM(degree)) = 2 AND TRIM(degree) BETWEEN '33' AND '64' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) "33-64",
       SUM(CASE WHEN (LENGTH(TRIM(degree)) = 2 AND TRIM(degree) BETWEEN '65' AND '99') OR
                     (LENGTH(TRIM(degree)) = 3 AND TRIM(degree) BETWEEN '100' AND '128') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) "65-128",
       SUM(CASE WHEN LENGTH(TRIM(degree)) = 3 AND TRIM(degree) BETWEEN '129' AND '256' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) "129-256",
       SUM(CASE WHEN LENGTH(TRIM(degree)) = 3 AND TRIM(degree) BETWEEN '257' AND '512' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) "257-512",
       SUM(CASE WHEN (LENGTH(TRIM(degree)) = 3 AND TRIM(degree) > '512') OR
                     (LENGTH(TRIM(degree)) > 3 AND TRIM(degree) != 'DEFAULT') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) "HIGHER"
  FROM dba_tables x
 WHERE owner NOT IN ('ANONYMOUS','APEX_030200','APEX_040000','APEX_040200','APEX_180200','APEX_SSO','APPQOSSYS','CTXSYS','DBSNMP','DIP','EXFSYS','FLOWS_FILES','MDSYS','OLAPSYS','ORACLE_OCM','ORDDATA','ORDPLUGINS','ORDSYS','OUTLN','OWBSYS')
   AND owner NOT IN ('SI_INFORMTN_SCHEMA','SQLTXADMIN','SQLTXPLAIN','SYS','SYSMAN','SYSTEM','TRCANLZR','WMSYS','XDB','XS$NULL','PERFSTAT','STDBYPERF','MGDSYS','OJVMSYS','GSMADMIN_INTERNAL')
HAVING COUNT(*) > SUM(CASE WHEN TRIM(degree) IN ('0', '1') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
 GROUP BY
       --con_id,
       owner
)
SELECT x.*
       --,c.name con_name
  FROM x
       --LEFT OUTER JOIN v$containers c ON c.con_id = x.con_id
 ORDER BY
       --x.con_id,
       x.owner;

sqls.name: DOP on indexes
sqls.description: [5.4] Same reading for indexes (an index with DOP > 1 is usually leftover from a parallel rebuild).
sqls.sql:
WITH x as (
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 2a.92 */
       --con_id,
       owner,
       SUM(CASE WHEN TRIM(degree) = 'DEFAULT' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) "DEFAULT",
       SUM(CASE WHEN TRIM(degree) = '0' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) "0",
       SUM(CASE WHEN TRIM(degree) = '1' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) "1",
       SUM(CASE WHEN TRIM(degree) = '2' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) "2",
       SUM(CASE WHEN TRIM(degree) IN ('3', '4') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) "3-4",
       SUM(CASE WHEN TRIM(degree) IN ('5', '6', '7', '8') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) "5-8",
       SUM(CASE WHEN TRIM(degree) IN ('9', '10', '11', '12', '13', '14', '15', '16') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) "9-16",
       SUM(CASE WHEN LENGTH(TRIM(degree)) = 2 AND TRIM(degree) BETWEEN '17' AND '32' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) "17-32",
       SUM(CASE WHEN LENGTH(TRIM(degree)) = 2 AND TRIM(degree) BETWEEN '33' AND '64' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) "33-64",
       SUM(CASE WHEN (LENGTH(TRIM(degree)) = 2 AND TRIM(degree) BETWEEN '65' AND '99') OR
                     (LENGTH(TRIM(degree)) = 3 AND TRIM(degree) BETWEEN '100' AND '128') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) "65-128",
       SUM(CASE WHEN LENGTH(TRIM(degree)) = 3 AND TRIM(degree) BETWEEN '129' AND '256' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) "129-256",
       SUM(CASE WHEN LENGTH(TRIM(degree)) = 3 AND TRIM(degree) BETWEEN '257' AND '512' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) "257-512",
       SUM(CASE WHEN (LENGTH(TRIM(degree)) = 3 AND TRIM(degree) > '512') OR
                     (LENGTH(TRIM(degree)) > 3 AND TRIM(degree) != 'DEFAULT') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) "HIGHER"
  FROM dba_indexes
 WHERE owner NOT IN ('ANONYMOUS','APEX_030200','APEX_040000','APEX_040200','APEX_180200','APEX_SSO','APPQOSSYS','CTXSYS','DBSNMP','DIP','EXFSYS','FLOWS_FILES','MDSYS','OLAPSYS','ORACLE_OCM','ORDDATA','ORDPLUGINS','ORDSYS','OUTLN','OWBSYS')
   AND owner NOT IN ('SI_INFORMTN_SCHEMA','SQLTXADMIN','SQLTXPLAIN','SYS','SYSMAN','SYSTEM','TRCANLZR','WMSYS','XDB','XS$NULL','PERFSTAT','STDBYPERF','MGDSYS','OJVMSYS','GSMADMIN_INTERNAL')
   AND index_type != 'LOB'
 GROUP BY
       --con_id,
       owner
HAVING COUNT(*) > SUM(CASE WHEN TRIM(degree) IN ('0', '1') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
)
SELECT x.*
       --,c.name con_name
  FROM x
       --LEFT OUTER JOIN v$containers c ON c.con_id = x.con_id
 ORDER BY
       --x.con_id,
       x.owner;

sqls.name: SQL using Literals (by count)
sqls.description: [5.5] Signatures with 100+ cursors caused by literals (gv$sql). Top N = bind-variable candidates; risk: hard parses, shared pool pressure, latch contention.
sqls.sql:
WITH
lit AS (
SELECT /*+  MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE  */ /* 2a.115 */
       --con_id,
       force_matching_signature, COUNT(*) cnt, MIN(sql_id) min_sql_id, MAX(sql_id) max_sql_id
  FROM gv$sql
 WHERE force_matching_signature > 0
   AND UPPER(sql_text) NOT LIKE '%EDB360%'
 GROUP BY
       --con_id,
       force_matching_signature
HAVING COUNT(*) > 99
)
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 2a.115 */
       DISTINCT lit.cnt, s.force_matching_signature,
       --s.con_id,
       s.parsing_schema_name owner,
       CASE WHEN o.object_name IS NOT NULL THEN o.object_name||'('||s.program_line#||')' END source,
       lit.min_sql_id,
       lit.max_sql_id,
       s.sql_text
	   --,c.name con_name
  FROM lit
       --LEFT OUTER JOIN v$containers c ON c.con_id = lit.con_id
      ,gv$sql s
       LEFT OUTER JOIN dba_objects o
                    ON o.object_id = s.program_id
                    --AND o.con_id = s.con_id
 WHERE s.force_matching_signature = lit.force_matching_signature
   AND s.sql_id = lit.min_sql_id
   --AND s.con_id = lit.con_id
 ORDER BY
       lit.cnt DESC,
	   --s.con_id,
	   s.force_matching_signature;

sqls.name: Top SQL by duplicates
sqls.description: [5.5] Top 100 duplicated SQL by FORCE_MATCHING_SIGNATURE with gets/reads/time and % of the cache totals. Name the worst offenders with numbers.
sqls.sql:
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 2a.125 */
   FORCE_MATCHING_SIGNATURE,
   duplicate_count,
   min_sql_id,
   max_sql_id,
   executions,
   buffer_gets,
   buffer_gets_per_exec,
   disk_reads,
   disk_reads_per_exec,
   rows_processed,
   rows_processed_per_exec,
   elapsed_seconds,
   elapsed_seconds_per_exec,
   pct_total_buffer_gets,
   pct_total_disk_reads,
   min_sql_text
   --,c.name con_name
from
  (SELECT
      --con_id,
      FORCE_MATCHING_SIGNATURE,
      count(*) duplicate_count,
      min(sql_id) min_sql_id,
      max(sql_id) max_sql_id,
      sum(executions) executions,
      sum(buffer_gets) buffer_gets,
      ROUND(sum(buffer_gets)/greatest(sum(executions),1)) buffer_gets_per_exec,
      sum(disk_reads) disk_reads,
      ROUND(sum(disk_reads)/greatest(sum(executions),1)) disk_reads_per_exec,
      sum(rows_processed) rows_processed,
      ROUND(sum(rows_processed)/greatest(sum(executions),1)) rows_processed_per_exec,
      round(sum(elapsed_time)/1000000, 3) elapsed_seconds,
      ROUND(sum(elapsed_time)/1000000/greatest(sum(executions),1), 3) elapsed_seconds_per_exec,
      ROUND(sum(buffer_gets)*100/(SELECT GREATEST(SUM(buffer_gets),1) FROM gv$sql), 1) pct_total_buffer_gets,
      ROUND(sum(disk_reads)*100/(SELECT GREATEST(SUM(disk_reads),1) FROM gv$sql), 1) pct_total_disk_reads,
      MIN(sql_text) min_sql_text,
      rank() over (ORDER BY count(*) desc nulls last) AS sql_rank
   from
      gv$sql
   WHERE
      FORCE_MATCHING_SIGNATURE <> 0 AND
      FORCE_MATCHING_SIGNATURE <> EXACT_MATCHING_SIGNATURE
   group by
      --con_id,
	  FORCE_MATCHING_SIGNATURE
   ORDER BY
      count(*) desc
  ) v1
  --LEFT OUTER JOIN v$containers c ON c.con_id = v1.con_id
WHERE
   sql_rank < 101;

sqls.description: [5.5] Open cursors per session (descending). Compare the top against the open_cursors parameter; close to the limit = ORA-01000 risk.

sqls.name: Session Cursor Cache Misses
sqls.description: [5.5] Sessions with session cursor cache misses; many misses suggest session_cached_cursors is low for the application's profile.
sqls.sql:
WITH
session_cache AS (
SELECT /*+  MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE  */ /* 2a.121 */
       p.value - c.value session_cache_misses,
       c.value session_cache_hits,
       p.value total_parse_count,
       --c.con_id,
       c.inst_id,
       c.sid
  FROM gv$sesstat c,

       gv$sesstat p,
       gv$statname n2
 WHERE n1.inst_id = c.inst_id
   AND n1.statistic# = c.statistic#
   AND n1.name = 'session cursor cache hits'
   AND n2.inst_id = p.inst_id
   AND n2.statistic# = p.statistic#
   AND n2.name = 'parse count (total)'
   AND p.inst_id = c.inst_id
   AND p.sid = c.sid
   --AND p.con_id = c.con_id
)
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 2a.121 */
       x.session_cache_misses,
       x.session_cache_hits,
       x.total_parse_count,
       --x.con_id,
       x.inst_id,
       x.sid,
       s.serial#,
       s.username,
       s.machine,
       s.program,
       s.module,
       s.action
	   --,c.name con_name

       --LEFT OUTER JOIN v$containers c ON c.con_id = x.con_id

sqls.name: Non-indexed FK Constraints
sqls.description: [5.6] FKs without an index: child-table locks on parent update/delete and poor joins. Recommend indexing FKs of busy tables.
sqls.sql:
WITH
ref_int_constraints AS (
SELECT /*+  MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE  */ /* 2a.65 */
       --col.con_id,
       col.owner,
       col.table_name,
       col.constraint_name,
       con.status,
       con.r_owner,
       con.r_constraint_name,
       COUNT(*) col_cnt,
       MAX(CASE col.position WHEN 01 THEN col.column_name END) col_01,
       MAX(CASE col.position WHEN 02 THEN col.column_name END) col_02,
       MAX(CASE col.position WHEN 03 THEN col.column_name END) col_03,
       MAX(CASE col.position WHEN 04 THEN col.column_name END) col_04,
       MAX(CASE col.position WHEN 05 THEN col.column_name END) col_05,
       MAX(CASE col.position WHEN 06 THEN col.column_name END) col_06,
       MAX(CASE col.position WHEN 07 THEN col.column_name END) col_07,
       MAX(CASE col.position WHEN 08 THEN col.column_name END) col_08,
       MAX(CASE col.position WHEN 09 THEN col.column_name END) col_09,
       MAX(CASE col.position WHEN 10 THEN col.column_name END) col_10,
       MAX(CASE col.position WHEN 11 THEN col.column_name END) col_11,
       MAX(CASE col.position WHEN 12 THEN col.column_name END) col_12,
       MAX(CASE col.position WHEN 13 THEN col.column_name END) col_13,
       MAX(CASE col.position WHEN 14 THEN col.column_name END) col_14,
       MAX(CASE col.position WHEN 15 THEN col.column_name END) col_15,
       MAX(CASE col.position WHEN 16 THEN col.column_name END) col_16,
       par.owner parent_owner,
       par.table_name parent_table_name,
       par.constraint_name parent_constraint_name
  FROM dba_constraints  con,
       dba_cons_columns col,
       dba_constraints  par
 WHERE con.constraint_type = 'R'
   AND con.owner NOT IN ('ANONYMOUS','APEX_030200','APEX_040000','APEX_040200','APEX_180200','APEX_SSO','APPQOSSYS','CTXSYS','DBSNMP','DIP','EXFSYS','FLOWS_FILES','MDSYS','OLAPSYS','ORACLE_OCM','ORDDATA','ORDPLUGINS','ORDSYS','OUTLN','OWBSYS')
   AND con.owner NOT IN ('SI_INFORMTN_SCHEMA','SQLTXADMIN','SQLTXPLAIN','SYS','SYSMAN','SYSTEM','TRCANLZR','WMSYS','XDB','XS$NULL','PERFSTAT','STDBYPERF','MGDSYS','OJVMSYS','GSMADMIN_INTERNAL')
   --AND col.con_id = con.con_id
   AND col.owner = con.owner
   AND col.constraint_name = con.constraint_name
   AND col.table_name = con.table_name
   --AND par.con_id(+) = con.con_id
   AND par.owner(+) = con.r_owner
   AND par.constraint_name(+) = con.r_constraint_name
 GROUP BY
       --col.con_id,
       col.owner,
       col.constraint_name,
       col.table_name,
       con.status,
       con.r_owner,
       con.r_constraint_name,
       par.owner,
       par.constraint_name,
       par.table_name
),
ref_int_indexes AS (
SELECT /*+  MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE  */ /* 2a.65 */
       --r.con_id,
       r.owner,
       r.constraint_name,
       c.table_owner,
       c.table_name,
       c.index_owner,
       c.index_name,
       r.col_cnt
  FROM ref_int_constraints r,
       dba_ind_columns c,
       dba_indexes i
 WHERE c.table_owner = r.owner
   AND c.table_name = r.table_name
   --AND c.con_id = r.con_id
   AND c.column_position <= r.col_cnt
   AND c.column_name IN (r.col_01, r.col_02, r.col_03, r.col_04, r.col_05, r.col_06, r.col_07, r.col_08,
                         r.col_09, r.col_10, r.col_11, r.col_12, r.col_13, r.col_14, r.col_15, r.col_16)
   --AND i.con_id = c.con_id
   AND i.owner = c.index_owner
   AND i.index_name = c.index_name
   AND i.table_owner = c.table_owner
   AND i.table_name = c.table_name
   AND i.index_type != 'BITMAP'
 GROUP BY
       --r.con_id,
       r.owner,
       r.constraint_name,
       c.table_owner,
       c.table_name,
       c.index_owner,
       c.index_name,
       r.col_cnt
HAVING COUNT(*) = r.col_cnt
)
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 2a.65 */
       x.*
       --,c.name con_name
  FROM ref_int_constraints x
       --LEFT OUTER JOIN v$containers c ON c.con_id = x.con_id
 WHERE NOT EXISTS (
SELECT NULL
  FROM ref_int_indexes i
 WHERE i.owner = x.owner
   --AND i.con_id = x.con_id
   AND i.constraint_name = x.constraint_name)
 ORDER BY
       1, 2, 3
       --, x.con_id;

sqls.name: Redundant Indexes
sqls.description: [5.6] Indexes whose column list is a prefix of another index: extra cost on every DML with no read benefit. Recommend evaluating removal (INVISIBLE first, monitor, then drop) with the application vendor's approval.
sqls.sql:
WITH
indexed_columns AS (
SELECT /*+  MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE  */ /* 2a.75 */
       --col.con_id,
       col.index_owner,
       col.index_name,
       col.table_owner,
       col.table_name,
       idx.index_type,
       idx.uniqueness,
       MAX(CASE col.column_position WHEN 01 THEN      col.column_name END)||
       MAX(CASE col.column_position WHEN 02 THEN ':'||col.column_name END)||
       MAX(CASE col.column_position WHEN 03 THEN ':'||col.column_name END)||
       MAX(CASE col.column_position WHEN 04 THEN ':'||col.column_name END)||
       MAX(CASE col.column_position WHEN 05 THEN ':'||col.column_name END)||
       MAX(CASE col.column_position WHEN 06 THEN ':'||col.column_name END)||
       MAX(CASE col.column_position WHEN 07 THEN ':'||col.column_name END)||
       MAX(CASE col.column_position WHEN 08 THEN ':'||col.column_name END)||
       MAX(CASE col.column_position WHEN 09 THEN ':'||col.column_name END)||
       MAX(CASE col.column_position WHEN 10 THEN ':'||col.column_name END)||
       MAX(CASE col.column_position WHEN 11 THEN ':'||col.column_name END)||
       MAX(CASE col.column_position WHEN 12 THEN ':'||col.column_name END)||
       MAX(CASE col.column_position WHEN 13 THEN ':'||col.column_name END)||
       MAX(CASE col.column_position WHEN 14 THEN ':'||col.column_name END)||
       MAX(CASE col.column_position WHEN 15 THEN ':'||col.column_name END)||
       MAX(CASE col.column_position WHEN 16 THEN ':'||col.column_name END)
       indexed_columns
  FROM dba_ind_columns col,
       dba_indexes idx
 WHERE col.table_owner NOT IN ('ANONYMOUS','APEX_030200','APEX_040000','APEX_040200','APEX_180200','APEX_SSO','APPQOSSYS','CTXSYS','DBSNMP','DIP','EXFSYS','FLOWS_FILES','MDSYS','OLAPSYS','ORACLE_OCM','ORDDATA','ORDPLUGINS','ORDSYS','OUTLN','OWBSYS')
   AND col.table_owner NOT IN ('SI_INFORMTN_SCHEMA','SQLTXADMIN','SQLTXPLAIN','SYS','SYSMAN','SYSTEM','TRCANLZR','WMSYS','XDB','XS$NULL','PERFSTAT','STDBYPERF','MGDSYS','OJVMSYS','GSMADMIN_INTERNAL')
   --AND idx.con_id = col.con_id
   AND idx.owner = col.index_owner
   AND idx.index_name = col.index_name
 GROUP BY
       --col.con_id,
       col.index_owner,
       col.index_name,
       col.table_owner,
       col.table_name,
       idx.index_type,
       idx.uniqueness
)
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 2a.75 */
       --r.con_id,
       r.table_owner,
       r.table_name,
       r.index_type,
       r.index_name||' ('||r.indexed_columns||')' redundant_index,
       i.index_name||' ('||i.indexed_columns||')' superset_index
       --,c.name con_name
  FROM indexed_columns r,
       indexed_columns i
       --LEFT OUTER JOIN v$containers c ON c.con_id = i.con_id
 WHERE i.table_owner = r.table_owner
   --AND i.con_id = r.con_id
   AND i.table_name = r.table_name
   AND i.index_type = r.index_type
   AND i.index_name != r.index_name
   AND i.indexed_columns LIKE r.indexed_columns||':%'
   AND r.uniqueness = 'NONUNIQUE'
 ORDER BY
       --r.con_id,
       r.table_owner,
       r.table_name,
       r.index_name,
       i.index_name;

WITH x as (

sqls.sql:
WITH k as (

FROM   dba_part_key_columns k
union all

FROM   dba_subpart_key_columns k
)
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 2a.85 */
       --i.con_id,

,      i.owner index_owner
,      i.index_name
,      i.index_type
,      'Partition' part_level
,      pi.locality
,      pi.partitioning_type
,      pi.partition_count
,      k.column_position part_column_position
,      k.column_name part_column_name

AND    pi.owner = i.owner
AND    pi.index_name = i.index_name
AND    pi.table_name = i.table_name

       ROUND(100 * (s.last_number - s.min_value) / GREATEST((s.max_value - s.min_value), 1), 1) percent_used, /* requested by Mike Moehlman */
       s.*
       --,c.name con_name
  FROM dba_sequences s
       --LEFT OUTER JOIN v$containers c ON c.con_id = s.con_id
 WHERE s.sequence_owner not in ('ANONYMOUS','APEX_030200','APEX_040000','APEX_040200','APEX_180200','APEX_SSO','APPQOSSYS','CTXSYS','DBSNMP','DIP','EXFSYS','FLOWS_FILES','MDSYS','OLAPSYS','ORACLE_OCM','ORDDATA','ORDPLUGINS','ORDSYS','OUTLN','OWBSYS')

sqls.name: Database Size on Disk
sqls.description: [5.7] On-disk size per file type (data/temp/log/control) and total.
sqls.sql:
WITH
sizes AS (
SELECT /*+  MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE  */ /* 1e.58 */
       'Data' file_type,
       SUM(bytes) bytes
  FROM v$datafile
 UNION ALL
SELECT 'Temp' file_type,
       SUM(bytes) bytes
  FROM v$tempfile
 UNION ALL
SELECT 'Log' file_type,
       SUM(bytes) * MAX(members) bytes
  FROM v$log
 UNION ALL
SELECT 'Control' file_type,
       SUM(block_size * file_size_blks) bytes
  FROM v$controlfile
),
dbsize AS (
SELECT /*+  MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE  */ /* 1e.58 */
       'Total' file_type,
       SUM(bytes) bytes
  FROM sizes
)
SELECT d.dbid,
       d.name db_name,
       s.file_type,
       s.bytes,
       ROUND(s.bytes/POWER(10,9),3) gb,
       CASE
       WHEN s.bytes > POWER(10,15) THEN ROUND(s.bytes/POWER(10,15),3)||' P'
       WHEN s.bytes > POWER(10,12) THEN ROUND(s.bytes/POWER(10,12),3)||' T'
       WHEN s.bytes > POWER(10,9) THEN ROUND(s.bytes/POWER(10,9),3)||' G'
       WHEN s.bytes > POWER(10,6) THEN ROUND(s.bytes/POWER(10,6),3)||' M'
       WHEN s.bytes > POWER(10,3) THEN ROUND(s.bytes/POWER(10,3),3)||' K'
       WHEN s.bytes > 0 THEN s.bytes||' B' END display
  FROM v$database d,
       sizes s
 UNION ALL
SELECT d.dbid,
       d.name db_name,
       s.file_type,
       s.bytes,
       ROUND(s.bytes/POWER(10,9),3) gb,
       CASE
       WHEN s.bytes > POWER(10,15) THEN ROUND(s.bytes/POWER(10,15),3)||' P'

       WHEN s.bytes > POWER(10,6) THEN ROUND(s.bytes/POWER(10,6),3)||' M'
       WHEN s.bytes > POWER(10,3) THEN ROUND(s.bytes/POWER(10,3),3)||' K'

  FROM v$database d,

sqls.name: Tablespace Usage
sqls.description: [5.7] Usage per tablespace considering MAXSIZE (autoextend). High usage of the possible maximum = a finding with proportional urgency; ignore a high % when plenty of autoextend room remains.
sqls.sql:
WITH
files AS (
SELECT /*+  MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE  */ /* 2b.141 */
       --con_id,
       tablespace_name,
       SUM(DECODE(autoextensible, 'YES', maxbytes, bytes)) / POWER(10,9) Max_size_gb,
       SUM( bytes) / POWER(10,9) Size_gb
  FROM dba_data_files
 GROUP BY
       --con_id,
       tablespace_name
),
segments AS (
SELECT /*+  MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE  */ /* 2b.141 */
       --con_id,
	   tablespace_name,
       SUM(bytes) / POWER(10,9) used_gb
  FROM dba_segments
 WHERE 'Y' = 'Y'
 GROUP BY
       --con_id,
       tablespace_name
),
tablespaces AS (
SELECT /*+  MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE  */ /* 2b.141 */
       --files.con_id,
       files.tablespace_name,
       ROUND(files.size_gb, 1) size_gb,
       ROUND(segments.used_gb, 1) used_gb,
       ROUND(100 * segments.used_gb / files.size_gb, 1) pct_used,
       ROUND(files.max_size_gb, 1) max_size_gb
  FROM files,
       segments
 WHERE files.size_gb > 0
   AND files.tablespace_name = segments.tablespace_name(+)
   --AND files.con_id = segments.con_id(+)
 ORDER BY
       --files.con_id,
       files.tablespace_name
),
total AS (
SELECT /*+  MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE  */ /* 2b.141 */
       'Total' tablespace_name,
       SUM(size_gb) size_gb,
       SUM(used_gb) used_gb,
       ROUND(100 * SUM(used_gb) / SUM(size_gb), 1) pct_used,
       sum(max_size_gb) max_size_gb
  FROM tablespaces
)
SELECT --con_id,
       tablespace_name,
       size_gb,
       used_gb,
       pct_used,
       max_size_gb
  FROM tablespaces
 UNION ALL
SELECT --NULL,
       tablespace_name,
       size_gb,
       used_gb,
       pct_used,
       max_size_gb
  FROM total;

sqls.name: Largest 200 Objects
sqls.description: [5.7] Top 200 segments with cumulative %. Name the largest and the concentration (e.g. top 20 = X% of the database).
sqls.sql:
WITH schema_object AS (
SELECT /*+  MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE  */ /* 2b.155 */
       --con_id,
       segment_type,
       owner,
       segment_name,
       tablespace_name,
       COUNT(*) segments,
       SUM(extents) extents,
       SUM(blocks) blocks,
       SUM(bytes) bytes
  FROM dba_segments
 WHERE 'Y' = 'Y'
 GROUP BY
       --con_id,
       segment_type,
       owner,
       segment_name,
       tablespace_name
), totals AS (
SELECT /*+  MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE  */ /* 2b.155 */
       SUM(segments) segments,
       SUM(extents) extents,
       SUM(blocks) blocks,
       SUM(bytes) bytes
  FROM schema_object
), top_200_pre AS (
SELECT /*+  MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE  */ /* 2b.155 */
       ROWNUM rank, v1.*
       FROM (
SELECT --so.con_id,
       so.segment_type,
       so.owner,
       so.segment_name,
       so.tablespace_name,
       so.segments,
       so.extents,
       so.blocks,
       so.bytes,
       ROUND((so.segments / t.segments) * 100, 3) segments_perc,
       ROUND((so.extents / t.extents) * 100, 3) extents_perc,
       ROUND((so.blocks / t.blocks) * 100, 3) blocks_perc,
       ROUND((so.bytes / t.bytes) * 100, 3) bytes_perc
  FROM schema_object so,
       totals t
 ORDER BY
       bytes_perc DESC NULLS LAST
) v1
 WHERE ROWNUM < 201
), top_200 AS (
SELECT p.*,
       (SELECT object_id
          FROM dba_objects o
         WHERE o.object_type = p.segment_type
		   --AND o.con_id = p.con_id
           AND o.owner = p.owner
           AND o.object_name = p.segment_name
           AND o.object_type NOT LIKE '%PARTITION%') object_id,
       (SELECT data_object_id
          FROM dba_objects o
         WHERE o.object_type = p.segment_type
           --AND o.con_id = p.con_id
           AND o.owner = p.owner
           AND o.object_name = p.segment_name
           AND o.object_type NOT LIKE '%PARTITION%') data_object_id,
       (SELECT SUM(p2.bytes_perc) FROM top_200_pre p2 WHERE p2.rank <= p.rank) bytes_perc_cum
  FROM top_200_pre p
), top_200_totals AS (
SELECT /*+  MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE  */ /* 2b.155 */
       SUM(segments) segments,
       SUM(extents) extents,
       SUM(blocks) blocks,
       SUM(bytes) bytes,
       SUM(segments_perc) segments_perc,
       SUM(extents_perc) extents_perc,
       SUM(blocks_perc) blocks_perc,
       SUM(bytes_perc) bytes_perc
  FROM top_200
), top_100_totals AS (
SELECT /*+  MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE  */ /* 2b.155 */
       SUM(segments) segments,
       SUM(extents) extents,
       SUM(blocks) blocks,
       SUM(bytes) bytes,
       SUM(segments_perc) segments_perc,
       SUM(extents_perc) extents_perc,
       SUM(blocks_perc) blocks_perc,
       SUM(bytes_perc) bytes_perc
  FROM top_200
 WHERE rank < 101
), top_20_totals AS (
SELECT /*+  MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE  */ /* 2b.155 */
       SUM(segments) segments,
       SUM(extents) extents,
       SUM(blocks) blocks,
       SUM(bytes) bytes,
       SUM(segments_perc) segments_perc,
       SUM(extents_perc) extents_perc,
       SUM(blocks_perc) blocks_perc,
       SUM(bytes_perc) bytes_perc
  FROM top_200
 WHERE rank < 21
)
SELECT v.rank,
       v.segment_type,
	   --v.con_id,
       v.owner,
       v.segment_name,
       v.object_id,
       v.data_object_id,
       v.tablespace_name,
       CASE
       WHEN v.segment_type LIKE 'INDEX%' THEN
         (SELECT i.table_name
            FROM dba_indexes i
           WHERE i.owner = v.owner
		     --AND i.con_id = v.con_id
		     AND i.index_name = v.segment_name)
       WHEN v.segment_type LIKE 'LOB%' THEN
         (SELECT l.table_name
            FROM dba_lobs l
           WHERE l.owner = v.owner
		     --AND l.con_id = v.con_id
		     AND l.segment_name = v.segment_name)
       END table_name,
       CASE
       WHEN v.segment_type LIKE 'LOB%' THEN
         (SELECT SUBSTR(l.column_name, 1, 128)
            FROM dba_lobs l
           WHERE l.owner = v.owner
             AND l.segment_name = v.segment_name)
       END lob_column,
       v.segments,
       v.extents,
       v.blocks,
       v.bytes,
       ROUND(v.bytes / POWER(10,9), 3) gb,
       LPAD(TO_CHAR(v.segments_perc, '990.000'), 7) segments_perc,
       LPAD(TO_CHAR(v.extents_perc, '990.000'), 7) extents_perc,
       LPAD(TO_CHAR(v.blocks_perc, '990.000'), 7) blocks_perc,
       LPAD(TO_CHAR(v.bytes_perc, '990.000'), 7) bytes_perc,
       LPAD(TO_CHAR(v.bytes_perc_cum, '990.000'), 7) perc_cum
	   --,c.name con_name
  FROM (
SELECT d.rank,
       d.segment_type,
	   --d.con_id,
       d.owner,
       d.segment_name,
       d.object_id,
       d.data_object_id,
       d.tablespace_name,
       d.segments,
       d.extents,
       d.blocks,
       d.bytes,
       d.segments_perc,
       d.extents_perc,
       d.blocks_perc,
       d.bytes_perc,
       d.bytes_perc_cum
  FROM top_200 d
 UNION ALL
SELECT TO_NUMBER(NULL) rank,
       NULL segment_type,
	   --NULL con_id,
       NULL owner,
       NULL segment_name,
       TO_NUMBER(NULL),
       TO_NUMBER(NULL),
       'TOP  20' tablespace_name,
       st.segments,
       st.extents,
       st.blocks,
       st.bytes,
       st.segments_perc,
       st.extents_perc,
       st.blocks_perc,
       st.bytes_perc,
       TO_NUMBER(NULL) bytes_perc_cum
  FROM top_20_totals st
 UNION ALL
SELECT TO_NUMBER(NULL) rank,
       NULL segment_type,
	   --NULL con_id,
       NULL owner,
       NULL segment_name,
       TO_NUMBER(NULL),
       TO_NUMBER(NULL),
       'TOP 100' tablespace_name,
       st.segments,
       st.extents,
       st.blocks,
       st.bytes,
       st.segments_perc,
       st.extents_perc,
       st.blocks_perc,
       st.bytes_perc,
       TO_NUMBER(NULL) bytes_perc_cum
  FROM top_100_totals st
 UNION ALL
SELECT TO_NUMBER(NULL) rank,
       NULL segment_type,
	   --NULL con_id,
       NULL owner,
       NULL segment_name,
       TO_NUMBER(NULL),
       TO_NUMBER(NULL),
       'TOP 200' tablespace_name,
       st.segments,
       st.extents,
       st.blocks,
       st.bytes,
       st.segments_perc,
       st.extents_perc,
       st.blocks_perc,
       st.bytes_perc,
       TO_NUMBER(NULL) bytes_perc_cum
  FROM top_200_totals st
 UNION ALL
SELECT TO_NUMBER(NULL) rank,
       NULL segment_type,
	   --NULL con_id,
       NULL owner,
       NULL segment_name,
       TO_NUMBER(NULL),
       TO_NUMBER(NULL),
       'TOTAL' tablespace_name,
       t.segments,
       t.extents,
       t.blocks,
       t.bytes,
       100 segemnts_perc,
       100 extents_perc,
       100 blocks_perc,
       100 bytes_perc,
       TO_NUMBER(NULL) bytes_perc_cum
  FROM totals t) v
  --LEFT OUTER JOIN v$containers c ON c.con_id = v.con_id;

sqls.name: SYSAUX Occupants
sqls.description: [5.7] SYSAUX occupants; an abnormally large occupant (e.g. SM/OPTSTAT) = a finding with a purge/retention action.
sqls.sql:
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 2b.153 */
       v.*, ROUND(v.space_usage_kbytes / POWER(10,6), 3) space_usage_gbs
  FROM v$sysaux_occupants v
 ORDER BY 1;

sqls.name: Segment Shrink Recommendations
sqls.description: [5.7] Segment Advisor recommendations (reclaimable space); list the top by reclaimable_space. May fail without EXECUTE on DBMS_SPACE.
sqls.sql:
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 2b.164 */
       *
FROM TABLE(dbms_space.asa_recommendations())
Where segment_owner not in ('ANONYMOUS','APEX_030200','APEX_040000','APEX_040200','APEX_180200','APEX_SSO','APPQOSSYS','CTXSYS','DBSNMP','DIP','EXFSYS','FLOWS_FILES','MDSYS','OLAPSYS','ORACLE_OCM','ORDDATA','ORDPLUGINS','ORDSYS','OUTLN','OWBSYS') and
   segment_owner not in ('SI_INFORMTN_SCHEMA','SQLTXADMIN','SQLTXPLAIN','SYS','SYSMAN','SYSTEM','TRCANLZR','WMSYS','XDB','XS$NULL','PERFSTAT','STDBYPERF','MGDSYS','OJVMSYS','GSMADMIN_INTERNAL')
order by reclaimable_space desc;

sqls.name: Objects in Recycle Bin
sqls.description: [5.7] Objects held in the recycle bin (retained space); purge if needed. If empty AND recyclebin=OFF in the parameters, raise enabling it in 5.2.
sqls.sql:
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 2b.165 */
       x.*
	   --,c.name con_name
  FROM dba_recyclebin x
       --LEFT OUTER JOIN v$containers c ON c.con_id = x.con_id
 WHERE x.owner NOT IN ('ANONYMOUS','APEX_030200','APEX_040000','APEX_040200','APEX_180200','APEX_SSO','APPQOSSYS','CTXSYS','DBSNMP','DIP','EXFSYS','FLOWS_FILES','MDSYS','OLAPSYS','ORACLE_OCM','ORDDATA','ORDPLUGINS','ORDSYS','OUTLN','OWBSYS')
   AND x.owner NOT IN ('SI_INFORMTN_SCHEMA','SQLTXADMIN','SQLTXPLAIN','SYS','SYSMAN','SYSTEM','TRCANLZR','WMSYS','XDB','XS$NULL','PERFSTAT','STDBYPERF','MGDSYS','OJVMSYS','GSMADMIN_INTERNAL')
 ORDER BY
       --x.con_id,
	   x.owner,
       x.object_name;

sqls.name: IO Statistics for DB Files
sqls.description: [5.7] I/O per file (v$iostat_file): average single-block latency per file; sustained above ~10-20 ms on a hot datafile = a storage finding.
sqls.sql:
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 2b.149 */
       x.*
	   --,c.name con_name
  FROM v$iostat_file x
       --LEFT OUTER JOIN v$containers c ON c.con_id = x.con_id
 ORDER BY
       1;

sqls.name: IO Outliers
sqls.description: [5.7] I/Os above 500 ms (v$io_outlier). Empty = ok; recurring entries = a storage finding.
sqls.sql:
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 2b.152 */
       *
  FROM v$io_outlier
 ORDER BY
       1;

sqls.name: Kernel IO Outliers
sqls.description: [5.7] Kernel-layer I/O outliers (v$kernel_io_outlier). Empty = ok.
sqls.sql:
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 2b.150 */
       *
  FROM v$kernel_io_outlier
 ORDER BY
       1;

sqls.name: Log Writer IO Outliers
sqls.description: [5.7] LGWR I/O outliers (v$lgwrio_outlier): they hit commit latency directly. Empty = ok.
sqls.sql:
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 2b.151 */
       *
  FROM v$lgwrio_outlier
 ORDER BY
       1;

sqls.name: Database Role & Protection
sqls.description: [5.8] Role (PRIMARY/STANDBY), log_mode, flashback, protection mode. NOARCHIVELOG in production = a critical finding.
sqls.sql:
SELECT database_role role, name, db_unique_name, platform_id, open_mode, log_mode, flashback_on, protection_mode, protection_level /* 2e.206 */
FROM v$database;

sqls.name: Force Logging
sqls.description: [5.8] force_logging and supplemental logging. With a standby/replication, force_logging NO = a critical finding (NOLOGGING operations corrupt the standby).
sqls.sql:
SELECT force_logging, remote_archive, supplemental_log_data_pk, supplemental_log_data_ui, switchover_status, dataguard_broker /* 2e.207 */
FROM v$database;

sqls.name: RMAN Backup Jobs
sqls.description: [5.8] RMAN jobs recorded in the controlfile. EMPTY = NO backup known to the database — a critical finding (or backup happens elsewhere; ask for confirmation). Recent FAILED = a finding; comment on window, duration and recommend periodic restore tests.
sqls.sql:
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 2d.187 */
       *
  FROM v$rman_backup_job_details
 --WHERE start_time >= (SYSDATE - 100)
 ORDER BY
       start_time DESC;

sqls.name: Block Corruption
sqls.description: [5.8] v$database_block_corruption. Empty = ok; ANY row = a critical finding with immediate action.

sqls.name: Block Change Tracking
sqls.description: [5.8] BCT speeds up incremental backups; DISABLED with an incremental strategy = a recommendation to enable.

sqls.name: Control Files
sqls.description: [5.8] Database control files. FEWER THAN 2 files = no multiplexing — a critical finding (losing the only control file takes the database down and complicates recovery); all on the same disk/filesystem (same path prefix) = equivalent risk; STATUS INVALID = a finding. Recommend multiplexing across at least 2 distinct disks.
sqls.sql:
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */
       name,
       status,
       is_recovery_dest_file,
       block_size,
       file_size_blks,
       ROUND(block_size * file_size_blks / POWER(10,6)) size_mb
  FROM v$controlfile
 ORDER BY
       name;

sqls.name: Redo Log Groups (v$log)
sqls.description: [5.8] Redo groups: size, status, archived. Groups too small for the switch rate (see the map) = a finding.
sqls.sql:
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 2d.195 */
     *
  FROM v$log
 ORDER BY 1, 2, 3, 4;

sqls.name: Redo Log Groups (summary)
sqls.description: [5.8] Summary view per thread/group (same source as the previous query).
sqls.sql:
SELECT thread#, group#, sequence#, bytes, archived ,status /* 2e.213 */
FROM v$log ORDER BY thread#, group#;

sqls.name: Redo Log Files
sqls.description: [5.8] Redo log members and paths. A group with a single member = no multiplexing (a finding); members on the same filesystem = risk. A member with STATUS INVALID or STALE = a finding.
sqls.sql:
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 2d.196 */
     *
  FROM v$logfile
 ORDER BY 1, 2, 3, 4;

sqls.name: Redo Log History (31 days)
sqls.description: [5.8] Switches per day over the last 31 days.
sqls.sql:
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 2d.197 */
 THREAD#, TO_CHAR(trunc(FIRST_TIME), 'YYYY-MON-DD') day, count(*)
FROM v$log_history
where FIRST_TIME >= (sysdate - 31)
group by rollup(THREAD#, trunc(FIRST_TIME))
order by THREAD#, trunc(FIRST_TIME);

sqls.name: Redo Switches Frequency Map
sqls.description: [5.8] Hour-by-hour switch map (last 14 days). A sustained average above ~6-12 switches/hour = undersized redo; recommend larger groups.
sqls.sql:
WITH
log AS (
SELECT /*+  MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE  */ /* 2d.198 */
       thread#,
       TO_CHAR(TRUNC(first_time), 'YYYY-MM-DD') yyyy_mm_dd,
       TO_CHAR(TRUNC(first_time), 'Dy') day,
       SUM(DECODE(TO_CHAR(first_time, 'HH24'), '00', 1, 0)) h00,
       SUM(DECODE(TO_CHAR(first_time, 'HH24'), '01', 1, 0)) h01,
       SUM(DECODE(TO_CHAR(first_time, 'HH24'), '02', 1, 0)) h02,
       SUM(DECODE(TO_CHAR(first_time, 'HH24'), '03', 1, 0)) h03,
       SUM(DECODE(TO_CHAR(first_time, 'HH24'), '04', 1, 0)) h04,
       SUM(DECODE(TO_CHAR(first_time, 'HH24'), '05', 1, 0)) h05,
       SUM(DECODE(TO_CHAR(first_time, 'HH24'), '06', 1, 0)) h06,
       SUM(DECODE(TO_CHAR(first_time, 'HH24'), '07', 1, 0)) h07,
       SUM(DECODE(TO_CHAR(first_time, 'HH24'), '08', 1, 0)) h08,
       SUM(DECODE(TO_CHAR(first_time, 'HH24'), '09', 1, 0)) h09,
       SUM(DECODE(TO_CHAR(first_time, 'HH24'), '10', 1, 0)) h10,
       SUM(DECODE(TO_CHAR(first_time, 'HH24'), '11', 1, 0)) h11,
       SUM(DECODE(TO_CHAR(first_time, 'HH24'), '12', 1, 0)) h12,
       SUM(DECODE(TO_CHAR(first_time, 'HH24'), '13', 1, 0)) h13,
       SUM(DECODE(TO_CHAR(first_time, 'HH24'), '14', 1, 0)) h14,
       SUM(DECODE(TO_CHAR(first_time, 'HH24'), '15', 1, 0)) h15,
       SUM(DECODE(TO_CHAR(first_time, 'HH24'), '16', 1, 0)) h16,
       SUM(DECODE(TO_CHAR(first_time, 'HH24'), '17', 1, 0)) h17,
       SUM(DECODE(TO_CHAR(first_time, 'HH24'), '18', 1, 0)) h18,
       SUM(DECODE(TO_CHAR(first_time, 'HH24'), '19', 1, 0)) h19,
       SUM(DECODE(TO_CHAR(first_time, 'HH24'), '20', 1, 0)) h20,
       SUM(DECODE(TO_CHAR(first_time, 'HH24'), '21', 1, 0)) h21,
       SUM(DECODE(TO_CHAR(first_time, 'HH24'), '22', 1, 0)) h22,
       SUM(DECODE(TO_CHAR(first_time, 'HH24'), '23', 1, 0)) h23,
       COUNT(*) per_day
  FROM v$log_history
 GROUP BY
       thread#,
       TRUNC(first_time)
 ORDER BY
       thread#,
       TRUNC(first_time) DESC NULLS LAST
),
ordered_log AS (
SELECT /*+  MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE  */ /* 2d.198 */
       ROWNUM row_num_noprint, log.*
  FROM log
),
min_set AS (
SELECT /*+  MATERIALIZE NO_MERGE  */ /* 2d.198 */
       thread#,
       MIN(row_num_noprint) min_row_num
  FROM ordered_log
 GROUP BY
       thread#
)
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 2d.198 */
       log.*
  FROM ordered_log log,
       min_set ms
 WHERE log.thread# = ms.thread#
   AND log.row_num_noprint < ms.min_row_num + 14
 ORDER BY
       log.thread#,
       log.yyyy_mm_dd DESC;

sqls.name: Redo Threads
sqls.description: [5.8] Instance redo threads. Informational.
sqls.sql:
SELECT thread#, instance, status /* 2e.209 */
FROM v$thread;

sqls.name: Archive Destinations
sqls.description: [5.8] Configured archive destinations per thread.
sqls.sql:
SELECT thread#, dest_id, destination, target, schedule, process /* 2e.215 */
 FROM gv$archive_dest gvad, gv$instance gvi
 WHERE gvad.inst_id = gvi.inst_id
   AND destination is NOT NULL
 ORDER BY thread#, dest_id;

sqls.name: Archive Destination Errors
sqls.description: [5.8] Errors per archive destination; any ERROR = a finding (a stuck archiver halts the database).
sqls.sql:
SELECT thread#, dest_id, gvad.status, error, fail_sequence /* 2e.217 */
 FROM gv$archive_dest gvad, gv$instance gvi
WHERE gvad.inst_id = gvi.inst_id
  AND destination is NOT NULL
ORDER BY thread#, dest_id;

sqls.name: Standby Destination Status
sqls.description: [5.8] Standby destination status (mode, protection, recovery). A gap or an unexpected mode = a finding.

sqls.name: Standby Redo Logs
sqls.description: [5.8] Standby redo logs; absence (or fewer than redo groups + 1 per thread) with Data Guard = a finding.
sqls.sql:

FROM v$standby_log order by thread#, group#;

sqls.name: NOLOGGING Objects
sqls.description: [5.8] NOLOGGING objects: direct-path loads become unrecoverable from backup and corrupt a standby. With backup/DR: recommend LOGGING (or database force_logging) and confirm the intent of each case.
sqls.sql:
WITH
objects AS (
SELECT 1 record_type,
       'TABLESPACE' object_type,
       --con_id,
       tablespace_name,
       NULL owner,
       NULL name,
       NULL column_name,
       NULL partition,
       NULL subpartition
  FROM dba_tablespaces
 WHERE logging = 'NOLOGGING'
   AND contents != 'TEMPORARY'
UNION ALL
SELECT 2 record_type,
       'TABLE' object_type,
       --con_id,
       tablespace_name,
       owner,
       table_name name,
       NULL column_name,
       NULL partition,
       NULL subpartition
  FROM dba_all_tables
 WHERE logging = 'NO'
   AND temporary = 'N'
UNION ALL
SELECT 3 record_type,
       'INDEX' object_type,
       --con_id,
       tablespace_name,
       owner,
       index_name name,
       NULL column_name,
       NULL partition,
       NULL subpartition
  FROM dba_indexes
 WHERE logging = 'NO'
   AND temporary = 'N'
UNION ALL
SELECT 4 record_type,
       'LOB' object_type,
       --con_id,
       tablespace_name,
       owner,
       table_name name,
       SUBSTR(column_name, 1, 30) column_name,
       NULL partition,
       NULL subpartition
  FROM dba_lobs
 WHERE logging = 'NO'
UNION ALL
SELECT 5 record_type,
       'TAB_PARTITION' object_type,
       --con_id,
       tablespace_name,
       table_owner owner,
       table_name name,
       NULL column_name,
       partition_name partition,
       NULL subpartition
  FROM dba_tab_partitions
 WHERE logging = 'NO'
UNION ALL
SELECT 6 record_type,
       'IND_PARTITION' object_type,
       --con_id,
       tablespace_name,
       index_owner owner,
       index_name name,
       NULL column_name,
       partition_name partition,
       NULL subpartition
  FROM dba_ind_partitions
 WHERE logging = 'NO'
UNION ALL
SELECT 7 record_type,
       'LOB_PARTITION' object_type,
       --con_id,
       tablespace_name,
       table_owner owner,
       table_name name,
       SUBSTR(column_name, 1, 30) column_name,
       partition_name partition,
       NULL subpartition
  FROM dba_lob_partitions
 WHERE logging = 'NO'
UNION ALL
SELECT 8 record_type,
       'TAB_SUBPARTITION' object_type,
       --con_id,
       tablespace_name,
       table_owner owner,
       table_name name,
       NULL column_name,
       partition_name partition,
       subpartition_name subpartition
  FROM dba_tab_subpartitions
 WHERE logging = 'NO'
UNION ALL
SELECT 9 record_type,
       'IND_SUBPARTITION' object_type,
       --con_id,
       tablespace_name,
       index_owner owner,
       index_name name,
       NULL column_name,
       partition_name partition,
       subpartition_name subpartition
  FROM dba_ind_subpartitions
 WHERE logging = 'NO'
UNION ALL
SELECT 10 record_type,
       'LOB_SUBPARTITION' object_type,
       --con_id,
       tablespace_name,
       table_owner owner,
       table_name name,
       SUBSTR(column_name, 1, 30) column_name,
       lob_partition_name partition,
       subpartition_name subpartition
  FROM dba_lob_subpartitions
 WHERE logging = 'NO'
)
SELECT x.object_type,
       --x.con_id,
	   x.tablespace_name,
       x.owner,
       x.name,
       x.column_name,
       x.partition,
       x.subpartition
	   --,c.name con_name
  FROM objects x
       --LEFT OUTER JOIN v$containers c ON c.con_id = x.con_id
 ORDER BY
       x.record_type,
       --con_id,
	   x.tablespace_name,
       x.owner,
       x.name,
       x.column_name,
       x.partition,
       x.subpartition;

sqls.name: Audit Parameters
sqls.description: [5.9] Audit parameters. audit_trail=NONE with no Unified Audit configured = a finding (no traceability for incident investigation); recommend at least object-change auditing.
sqls.sql:
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 1c.41 */
       inst_id, name "PARAMETER", value, isdefault, ismodified
  FROM gv$system_parameter2
 WHERE name LIKE '%audit%'
 ORDER BY 2,1,3;

sqls.name: Users with Sensitive Roles
sqls.description: [5.9] Users holding sensitive roles (DBA, RESOURCE, %ANY%, IMP/EXP_FULL...). Explain the risk of the main roles found and recommend least privilege (Privilege Analysis is free since 18c).
sqls.sql:
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 1b.29 */
       x.*
       --,c.name con_name
  FROM dba_role_privs x
       --LEFT OUTER JOIN v$containers c ON c.con_id = x.con_id
 WHERE (x.granted_role in
('AQ_ADMINISTRATOR_ROLE','DELETE_CATALOG_ROLE','DBA','DM_CATALOG_ROLE','EXECUTE_CATALOG_ROLE',
'EXP_FULL_DATABASE','GATHER_SYSTEM_STATISTICS','HS_ADMIN_ROLE','IMP_FULL_DATABASE',
   'JAVASYSPRIV','JAVA_ADMIN','JAVA_DEPLOY','LOGSTDBY_ADMINISTRATOR',
   'OEM_MONITOR','OLAP_DBA','RECOVERY_CATALOG_OWNER','SCHEDULER_ADMIN',
   'SELECT_CATALOG_ROLE','WM_ADMIN_ROLE','XDBADMIN','RESOURCE')
    or x.granted_role like '%ANY%')
   and x.grantee not in ('ANONYMOUS','APEX_030200','APEX_040000','APEX_040200','APEX_180200','APEX_SSO','APPQOSSYS','CTXSYS','DBSNMP','DIP','EXFSYS','FLOWS_FILES','MDSYS','OLAPSYS','ORACLE_OCM','ORDDATA','ORDPLUGINS','ORDSYS','OUTLN','OWBSYS')
   and x.grantee not in ('SI_INFORMTN_SCHEMA','SQLTXADMIN','SQLTXPLAIN','SYS','SYSMAN','SYSTEM','TRCANLZR','WMSYS','XDB','XS$NULL','PERFSTAT','STDBYPERF','MGDSYS','OJVMSYS','GSMADMIN_INTERNAL')
   and (x.grantee
       --,x.con_id
	   ) IN (SELECT u.username
	              --, u.con_id
		     FROM dba_users u)
order by x.grantee, x.granted_role
--,x.con_id;

sqls.name: Non-default System Grants
sqls.description: [5.9] System privileges granted to non-Oracle users/roles; review excess and dangerous privileges (ALTER SYSTEM, CREATE ANY...).
sqls.sql:
select  /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 1b.36 */
x.*
--,c.name con_name

sqls.name: Users with Inappropriate Tablespaces
sqls.description: [5.9] Users with default tablespace SYSTEM/SYSAUX or a wrong temporary; fix to avoid undue dictionary growth.
sqls.sql:
SELECT /*+  NO_MERGE  */ /* 1b.30 */
       x.*
       --,c.name con_name
FROM   dba_users x
       --LEFT OUTER JOIN v$containers c ON c.con_id = x.con_id, c
WHERE  (x.default_tablespace in ('SYSAUX','SYSTEM')
or (x.temporary_tablespace
   --,x.con_id
   ) not in
   (select t.tablespace_name
          --,t.con_id
   from dba_tablespaces t
   where t.contents = 'TEMPORARY'
   and t.status = 'ONLINE'))
and NVL((SELECT COUNT(*)
         FROM dba_tablespace_groups g, dba_tablespaces t
         WHERE g.group_name = x.temporary_tablespace
		 --AND g.con_id = x.con_id
		 --AND t.con_id = g.con_id
         AND t.tablespace_name = g.tablespace_name
         AND t.contents IN ('PERMANENT', 'UNDO')), 0) != 0

sqls.name: Alert Log (recent)
sqls.description: [5.10] Latest alert log messages (newest first; the prompt shows only the first rows — a sample). Look for ORA-, deadlocks, incomplete checkpoints, archiver stalls. Base statements only on what is shown.
sqls.sql:
SELECT
    time,
    alert
FROM (
    SELECT
        alert.record_id,
        alert.originating_timestamp AT TIME ZONE SESSIONTIMEZONE AS time,
        alert.message_text AS alert
    FROM
        v$diag_alert_ext alert
    ORDER BY
        alert.record_id DESC
    FETCH FIRST 2000 ROWS ONLY
)
ORDER BY
    record_id DESC;
